event: Wren wakes to the wrong bird: not the millwheel, but the basin's layered morning calls.
Green-gold light shimmers through the canopy gap above her tarp.
Day 2, she thinks; the wrongness is something to learn, not to fight.
She packs her bedroll the way her mother drilled her, and follows the smell of tea.
Theron has rebuilt the fire from last night's coals; he pours her a cup without a word.
The insect chorus ended before the birds began: 'That means the night was dry.'
The basin thrush calls in threes when the weather is steady; in fours, check the sky.
Wren says she will go south today, as far as feels sound.
Theron names the fen a mile south, the Mudgrass, where paths change faster.
He tells her to let Hadley come; Hadley knows the Mudgrass. He goes to his lean-to.
Hadley appears from the ferns, already muddy, bound for mirewillow bark.
He shows her a new ghost-elm root that spirals counter-clockwise.
Wren asks to see the tree's roots in place tomorrow. 'Yes,' says Hadley.
They walk south; the ghost elms grow older, and the oldest hum lowest.
Hadley says Theron knows how but never why; Hadley needs the why.
Wren offers to keep a list of things he cannot explain. 'The list is already long.'
Forty minutes south, [Wayfinder's Eye] shimmers on a ghost elm's root flare.
Fine moss threaded with silver lines follows the water's flow down the roots.
Hadley names it silvervein moss, which Hesta sells in Millhaven for a salve.
A discovery logs silvervein moss: +35 XP, and Herbalism activates.
She thinks of the blister her pack strap raised on her collarbone yesterday.
She takes less than a quarter of the mat, Theron's formula, and wraps it in cloth.
The fen arrives without warning; her boot sinks into mud.
Hadley crosses on the lighter ground: dark means water, light means root.
Hummocks crowned with pale-stemmed plants rise between amber, tea-colored water.
The Ashbrook runs here braided into channels over fine white gravel.
The river makes her think of her father, who measures it every spring and autumn.
The Shelf is fainter today but present, like the millwheel in her bones.
She finds the letter in her journal: she forgot to give it to Hadley.
Not guilt: the Thornwild arrived so loudly the letter slipped from her mind.
She moves the letter to her shirt pocket and starts sketching the river.
Upstream, Hadley strips mirewillow bark in long rolls, giving her space.
On her spirit lamp she heats river water in her tin cup to just below boiling.
She steeps the moss two minutes, as Hesta's hands taught her.
A thin cool gel clings to the cup; she presses it onto the blister.
The irritation eases, small and precise, at the blister and nowhere else.
Crafting record: crude Silvervein Salve, quality 38 of 100, +30 XP.

changes.note: Crafting: first Silvervein Salve, new recipe

event: ACHIEVEMENT UNLOCKED: First Creation, +1 DEX: 'You have begun.'
She notes the gel should be thicker and steeped longer; her hands set the ceiling.
She records the +1 DEX in her journal, as her father taught her.
The compass pulls: a clear, directed lean south, not the Thornwild's deviation.
She has reached Level 3, and [Lay the Path] gains Compass Sensitivity.

changes.note: Level 3 reached by the day's discoveries and the salve

event: Her father's compass now points to undiscovered features: SSW, about 200 meters.
The System has made the tool for finding roads a tool for finding what is off them.
She calls Hadley and shows him the needle's steady pull.
SSW lies a deep pool Theron calls the Eye; he never goes there, and never says why.
It is at the five-mile boundary, maybe just inside. 'Come with me,' she says.
The mirewillow ends, the ground firms, and there is the pool.
It is fifteen meters across, green-black, unrippled, ringed with shoulder-high reed-ferns.
[Wayfinder's Eye] does not shimmer; it focuses, sustained and deep.
The pool looks at her; she keeps the thought to herself.
Hadley, quiet, asks what she feels. 'Nothing wrong. I think it's waiting.'
The needle stills: she has arrived. 'For someone to notice it properly.'
A discovery logs the Warden's Eye, bond potential medium: +60 XP.

changes.note: Discovery: the Warden's Eye, significant location

event: 'This location has not been properly met.' 'Not today,' she says.
She needs more time to understand it, and will come back.
She sketches the pool, its plants, and the bearing from camp, and marks a question mark.
Hadley tells her the Rimfolk gathered at this pool on the seventeenth day.
His grandmother said the pool was where the forest was most itself.
Wren links the seventeenth day to the Crying Forest's cycle, and turns for home.
At the camp's edge, in the last amber light, she gives Hadley the letter.
He tucks it in his satchel: the twice-monthly run leaves in six days.
'You forgot to give it this morning.' 'I did.'
She forgets things when she pays attention to other things.
Theron watched her go south; Hadley thinks he is deciding: problem or talent.
'It's both,' Wren says.
Dinner in half an hour: Theron found young ghost-elm fungi this morning.
She follows Hadley to the fire, the Shelf in her chest like a carried lamp.
For now, she is home enough.
